mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D). Preserve the order of terms as stated.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence contains an equality between differences, e.g., "the number of apples that X has more than Y equals the difference between Z and W".
mathgap.example: Treating "X has more than Y" as an absolute difference |X‑Y| or swapping X and Y, losing the sign.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states "X has N apples" (or a similar direct count).
mathgap.example: Assuming the count stays unchanged even after later transfers that modify it.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more items than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer items than Y" as X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence uses the words "more" or "fewer" to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Writing Y = X + N instead of X = Y + N, thereby reversing the relationship.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, give each recipient half of the giver's items and set the giver's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence contains "splits all the apples she owns equally among A and B" (or similar).
mathgap.example: Dividing the apples but forgetting to zero‑out the original holder.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, using the current counts at that moment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence says "X gives N apples to Y" (or a similar transfer).
mathgap.example: Using the giver's original count instead of the count after earlier transfers, leading to an incorrect amount transferred.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known, substitute its numeric value into the equation to simplify and solve for the remaining unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving equations that involve signed differences and some of those differences have been previously determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving an equation like (A‑B) = (C‑D) unsolved even though (A‑B) is already known from an earlier statement.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts, not the initial ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem where the order of operations (transfers, splits, conditionals) matters.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a later statement that should reflect earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Preserve order in signed difference statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions the "difference between X and Y", treat it as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order as stated.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence describes a difference, e.g., "the difference between X and Y".
mathgap.example: Swapping the terms and interpreting it as Y − X, which changes the sign of the difference.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of apples that X has increases by a/b times", interpret it as a multiplication: X = X × (a/b). Do not add the fraction of the original amount.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses the phrase "increases by … times" with a fractional factor.
mathgap.example: Treating "increases by 3/2 times" as X = X + (3/2)X = (5/2)X instead of X = (3/2)X.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: When a conditional transfer statement appears (e.g., "If X has more than N apples, X will transfer their apples to Y"), evaluate the condition using X's current count at that point; if true, move all of X's apples to Y (X becomes 0, Y gains those apples).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement includes an "if" clause that governs a transfer of all apples.
mathgap.example: Always transferring X's apples to Y regardless of X's count, or never transferring even when the condition is satisfied.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses signed differences with absolute differences and may reverse the order of terms, losing the sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order and treat "difference between X and Y" as X − Y.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes transfers out of order, using outdated counts instead of the most recent values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Follow chronological evaluation; apply each transfer as it appears in the text.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats initial counts as immutable, overlooking later statements that modify them.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update counts after each transfer or split; treat explicit counts as starting values only.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the condition and either always or never applies the transfer.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate the condition based on the current count before applying the transfer.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by a/b times" as additive rather than multiplicative
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing is ambiguous; models may think "increase by" means adding the fraction of the original amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "increases by a/b times" as multiplication: X = X × (a/b).
